name: Jasper Pink
lede: Jasper Pink is a soft salmon-pink named for the stone jasper, and the English name ColorHub gives to a traditional Japanese color measured out by dye weight.

sections.title: A pink measured in dye, not stone
sections.body: Ridgway's 1912 atlas gives this swatch at plate XIII, hue 3′, tone d, filed by the 1955 ISCC-NBS system in block 26, a deep pink [1]. Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary records the same name from 1912 [1]. ColorHub's library pairs it with a Japanese name, ikkonzome (一斤染), literally "one-kin dye", naming the pale shade by the single kin, about 0.6 kilograms, of safflower dye used to produce it [2]. Its nearest library neighbor is [[alizarine-pink]], and the closest core app color is [[salmon]], over eight units away [1]. It leans than to the more orange [[salmon]], despite the app field naming salmon as its nearest core color [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this pink in only 4 of 23,781 paintings[3]. All four matches are French paintings from the nineteenth century, including an 1853 self-portrait by Louis Gustave Ricard and an 1880 still life of flowers [3]. With so few matches, this French, nineteenth-century lean may be coincidence rather than pattern [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, and a match this rare says little about where or how often the color was actually used [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors, not pigment identifications[3].
